sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A. No. 21526 of 2025 as it has been wrongly filed without taking into consideration pendency of I.A. No. 18168 of 2025.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 21526 of 2025 is dismissed as withdrawn with a cost of Rs.5,000/- to be paid in the account of High Court Legal Services Committee.
Heard on I.A. No. 18168 of 2025 , which is second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the sole appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
His earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn on 12.04.2024.

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 28.07.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge, S.C./ S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Sihore in Special Case No. 130 of 2020 whereby the appellant has been convicted under Section 376-D of IPC and sentenced to R.I.
for life, till the remainder of natural life, with fine of Rs.10,000/- and 2 CRA-10530-2023 also under Section 342 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs.1,000/- along with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the Dehati Nalisi (Ex. P/31), which was recorded on 23.10.2020 at about 20:05 hrs narrating the incident which had taken place on 10.01.2020 at about 11:30 p.m., violators of privacy have been named as Shivraj, Rambabu and Umashankar.

sentences.text: There are good chances of success of the appeal.
It is, therefore, prayed that sentence of the present appellant be suspended and he be granted bail.
Learned Government Advocate, on the other hand, opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, without commenting on the merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 18168 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 09.12.2025 and such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the 3 CRA-10530-2023 execution of remaining part of jail sentence imposed upon appellant Mukesh Ahirwar shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of the appeal.
C. C. as per rules.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL)
